brief.outcome: Launch a first cohort of an online course that teaches other photographers to price and sell wedding packages, and reach 100 paid course sales within four months, without promising income results.

ambition.goal_beyond: Photographers who buy the course use it, and the course can sell again after the first launch.
rungs: Build the course page, price and launch emails, and run one launch to your list and Instagram.

Test who will really pay before the whole course is built: who is in your 900 and 18,000, what price they accept, and what stops them. Launch to the group that responds, and report honestly against 100 sales.
Keep the course selling: a standing weekly check of sales, sources and refunds, plus a second cohort date, so a drop is caught early.
ambition.judge: Paid orders and refunds exported from the course platform's own sales records, and each source's sales counted from tagged links; not the owner's or our estimate.

brief.deliverable: A ready founding-cohort offer (course outline, price, sales page, launch emails, Instagram posts), the first launch run with your approval, and an honest sales readout against the 100-sale goal.

Launch sent and posted only with your yes for each action; ad spend stays within $1,000
Sales read from the platform's records against the 100-sale goal, with refunds and complaints
Lessons saved and a date set for the next cohort or a stop decision

answers.question: What do you do and what is the course about?
answers.answer: Wedding photographer with 12 years experience. Want to teach other photographers to price and sell wedding packages.

answers.question: What audience and assets do you have?
answers.answer: 18,000 Instagram followers, email list of 900 mostly past clients. I can record video myself.

answers.question: What does success look like and by when?
answers.answer: 100 course sales in the first launch, within four months.

answers.question: Budget, platform, limits and who decides?
answers.answer: No budget for ads beyond $1,000. No platform chosen yet. Do not promise income results. Keep data in this project. I decide.

answers.question: My guess for what should happen after the launch (ambition)
answers.answer: Accepted as the working guess: you want photographers who buy to use it, and the course to sell again. We aim to find who really buys before building everything, and report honestly against 100.

research.approach: Practitioners treat a first course launch as a demand test before a build. They define one concrete outcome for the buyer, set a real start date, and sell a founding cohort to the warm audience with a deadline, building the course a module ahead of the students. They check who the audience really is, because list size matters less than engaged buyers of this exact skill. They run a waitlist and value emails before cart opens, a short cart window with a real close, and a final-48-hour push. They keep claims honest (no typical-results implication from testimonials), keep email within the law, and read results against a rule set beforehand. When sales are low they talk to a handful of prospects to find out whether the problem is position, audience warmth or price. The owner's list is mostly past clients, who are couples and not photographers, so audience fit is the first thing to test.

sources.title: How to Sell an Online Course Before You Build It (Kajabi)
sources.note: Pre-sell steps: one concrete outcome, a real start date six to eight weeks out, sell to the existing list, decide in advance what counts as enough sales, build one module ahead, refund everyone if you cannot deliver. Vendor guidance, no benchmark data.

sources.title: Launch an online course (Ruzuku)
sources.note: Phases: 2 to 3 weeks pre-launch with a waitlist and value emails, a 5 to 7 day enrollment window with a 48-hour warning, then post-launch survey. Says timing and discount advice is not platform data. If sales are zero, contact 5 to 10 prospects personally.

sources.title: FTC Endorsement Guides: what people are asking
sources.note: Page shows no publication date; accessed 2026-11-03. Regulator guidance, current version revised 2023 (page itself is undated). Exceptional results in testimonials need clear statement of generally expected results; do not suppress negative reviews.

sources.title: CAN-SPAM Act: a compliance guide for business (FTC)
sources.note: Regulator rules: honest header, clear opt-out honoured within 10 business days, a physical postal address, penalties per email.

sources.title: Email sender guidelines (Google)
sources.note: Page shows no publication date; accessed 2026-11-03. Platform rules enforced from February 2024: SPF or DKIM for all senders, spam rate under 0.30% and ideally under 0.10%, one-click unsubscribe for marketing mail.

steps.name: Count who the warm audience really is
steps.why: List size is not buyer count. Past wedding clients are couples, so the number of photographers on the list and among followers sets the ceiling for sales.

steps.name: Scan rival photographer-business courses for price and promise
steps.why: A price and promise are judged against what the buyer can compare.

steps.name: Fix the claims and list rules before writing
steps.why: Earnings or booking claims need proof the owner does not have, and the list must be lawful to email.

steps.name: Choose one buyer outcome, price and real start date
steps.why: A concrete outcome, a founding-cohort price and a real start date make the offer testable and the urgency honest.

steps.name: Outline the course and brief module one
steps.why: Build one module ahead of the students and use their questions for the rest.

steps.name: Write the sales page, emails and posts
steps.why: A waitlist, value emails, cart-open sequence and a final-48-hour close, with objections answered and proof placed.

steps.name: Run the pre-sell, then the cart window, with tagged links
steps.why: Warm audience first with a real deadline; paid reach only after the warm result is read.

steps.name: Read sales against a rule set before launch; interview if low
steps.why: Decide in advance what counts as enough; if sales are zero, talk to 5 to 10 prospects to find the cause.

steps.name: Survey buyers and non-buyers, set the next cohort date
steps.why: Buyers' questions shape the course; a date for the next cohort keeps the audience moving.

pitfalls.text: Counting a list of past clients as a list of buyers when they are not photographers.
Building the whole course before testing demand, or rushing pre-launch.
Using testimonials or hints that imply typical income or booking results.
Emailing an older list without a clear opt-out or authentication, which raises spam complaints and hurts every later send.
Fake urgency; the deadline and start date must be real.

stages.name: Confirm the brief
stages.goal: Turn the owner's words into a measured goal, limits and what is unknown. Writes BRIEF.md.

stages.name: Count the audience and scan rival courses
stages.goal: Tag who on the list and followers is a photographer or likely buyer, read Instagram results for business posts, and record price and promise of five to ten rival courses.

checks.name: List total in the working copy matches the export's own row count exactly
Anyone not clearly a photographer is counted as unknown, never as a buyer
At least five rival courses with price, promise and date read

stages.name: Check the list and the claims rules
stages.goal: Check that the list can lawfully and safely be emailed and set the claims register: what may be said, what proof is needed, and what is banned (any income or booking promise).

checks.name: Each segment to be emailed has a recorded opt-in source, or is excluded from the send
Sending domain passes SPF or DKIM, has a one-click unsubscribe and a postal address in the footer
Claims are sorted into allowed, needs-proof and banned; no sentence implies typical income or bookings

stages.name: Can this audience reach 100 sales?
stages.goal: Turn the counts into funnel maths for the 100-sale goal, rank which groups to sell to first, and test the hypotheses about audience fit, reach, price and proof. State the gap to 100 honestly.

checks.name: Every hypothesis is SUPPORTED, REFUTED or UNKNOWN with the count behind it
Funnel maths shows a low, middle and high buy rate and the audience size needed for 100 sales at each; rates are labelled as assumptions
The main finding names a competing explanation

stages.name: Rank offer, price and launch shapes
stages.goal: Offer three to five ranked combinations of buyer outcome, founding-cohort price, start date and launch shape (waitlist, live workshop, direct pre-sell), each with the finding it rests on, expected effect, effort, confidence, risk and how it is measured.

checks.name: Every option cites the diagnosis finding it rests on
Every option states price, start date, sales needed for the goal, effort, confidence and risk
No option relies on an income or booking promise

stages.name: Owner chooses the offer
stages.goal: The owner picks the offer, price, start date and launch shape, and signs the success rule: how many sales or waitlist sign-ups by when mean go, adjust or stop. Ask why when the top option is passed over.

checks.name: Chosen and passed-over options are recorded with reasons
The go, adjust or stop rule has numbers and dates and is written before anything is sent

stages.name: Outline the course and brief module one
stages.goal: Turn the chosen promise into a short module outline and a recording brief for module one, so the owner can film one module ahead of the buyers.

checks.name: Each module maps to one skill the promise names, with a practice task the buyer does
No module description or outcome promises income or bookings
Every example the owner must supply is listed, none invented

stages.name: Write the sales page, emails and posts
stages.goal: Write the sales page, price display, waitlist and launch emails with a real close, answers to the buyer's doubts, and Instagram posts. Check every claim against the claims register before the owner sees it.

checks.name: Every claim is allowed in the claims register; zero sentences imply typical income or bookings
Every deadline and spot limit matches the start date and capacity the owner chose
Every email has a clear opt-out, a postal address and honest sender details
The top five buyer doubts each have an answer on the page

stages.name: Run the pre-sell and cart window
stages.goal: Register the launch as an experiment with its rule and tagged links, open the page, then send the waitlist and launch emails and post, one approved action at a time. Warm audience first.

checks.name: The launch rule and baseline are in experiments.jsonl before the first send
A test email and a test checkout work on a phone before the first real send
Every link carries a source tag so each channel's sales can be counted from orders
Spam complaints stay under 0.1% of sends after the first send, or sending pauses

stages.name: Optional paid reach test
stages.goal: Only if the warm result shows paid reach could pay back, set a small test to photographers within the $1,000 cap, ready for the owner to switch on.

checks.name: Total planned spend is at or under $1,000 and the daily cap is shown
The maximum cost per sale is set from the price and platform fees, and spend stops above it

stages.optional_when: The warm launch already reaches the goal, or the owner chooses not to spend.

stages.name: Read sales against the rule
stages.goal: Read paid orders, refunds and source tags from the platform's own export against the signed rule and the 100-sale goal. If sales are low, plan five to ten prospect calls to find the cause.

checks.name: Sales come from the platform export; owner-reported counts are labelled as reports
Refunds and complaints are shown beside sales
The verdict uses the rule signed before launch and says how far the result is from 100

stages.name: Keep what we learned and set the next date
stages.goal: Close the experiment, send the buyer and non-buyer survey, save rules with their scope, and set the next cohort date or a stop decision.

checks.name: The launch experiment is closed in experiments.jsonl with a verdict
Each saved rule says whether it applies to this launch, this business or any course
A next-cohort date or a stop decision is written

hypotheses.statement: Most of the 900 emails and many followers are couples and past clients, not photographers, so the buyer pool is small.
hypotheses.test: Tag the list by photographer yes, no or unknown; read Instagram audience data; run a one-question story poll.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Photographers on the list are fewer than 100 of the 900 (about one in nine), or the poll shows under 10% of responders are photographers.
hypotheses.refute_if: Photographers are at least 20% of the list and of poll responders.

hypotheses.statement: The warm audience alone cannot reach 100 sales at a plausible buy rate.
hypotheses.test: Funnel maths: photographers reachable times a low, middle and high buy rate (labelled as assumptions), compared to 100.
hypotheses.confirm_if: At the middle rate the reachable photographers give fewer than 100 sales.
hypotheses.refute_if: At the low rate the warm audience already gives 100 sales or more.

hypotheses.statement: The price is out of line with what rival courses charge and what the promise is worth to a working photographer.
hypotheses.test: Compare the candidate price with the rival scan and with one booking's value; ask five to ten photographers about price in short calls.
hypotheses.confirm_if: The price is above all rivals with a similar promise, or most called photographers say it is too high.
hypotheses.refute_if: The price sits within the rival range and most called photographers call it fair.

hypotheses.statement: Without income claims, buyers doubt the owner can teach selling; proof is missing.
hypotheses.test: Collect the top buyer doubts from the poll and calls; check which have honest proof on file (years, packages priced, work shown).
hypotheses.confirm_if: Three or more of the top five doubts have no allowed proof.
hypotheses.refute_if: Every top doubt has allowed proof ready to place on the page.

hypotheses.statement: The list is cold or not opted in for marketing, so emails go to spam or draw complaints.
hypotheses.test: Check opt-in source and last-engagement date; read complaint and bounce rates after the first small send.
hypotheses.confirm_if: More than 30% of the list has no recorded marketing opt-in, or complaints exceed 0.1% of the first send.
hypotheses.refute_if: Opt-in is recorded for at least 80% and complaints stay under 0.1%.

measurement.window: Waitlist 2 to 3 weeks, cart open 5 to 7 days, read daily during the cart, final readout 7 days after close; survey 30 days after delivery starts.
measurement.min_volume: A price or channel verdict only at 20 or more paid orders or 200 or more tagged clicks per channel; below that the verdict is INCONCLUSIVE.
measurement.stop_rule: Pause sending if spam complaints reach 0.1% of sends; stop paid spend if cost per sale passes the break-even set at decision or the $1,000 cap is reached; otherwise run the full window.
